question: **Find the part of the sentence that contains an error**: The official, addressing the press yesterday, (1)/ claimed that the matter had been resolved (2)/ though no evidences supporting the statement (3)/ was ever made available. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the plural form "**evidences**."
 
• In English grammar, "**evidence**" is an uncountable (or mass) noun.
 
• Uncountable nouns cannot be counted individually and do not take a plural "-s" suffix.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**no evidence**," ensuring grammatical correctness and proper agreement with the singular verb "was" later in the sentence.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The official, addressing the press yesterday, claimed that the matter had been resolved though no **evidence supporting the statement** was ever made available."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "The official, addressing the press yesterday," **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and properly uses a participial phrase.
 
• **2: "claimed that the matter had been resolved"** – This part is grammatically correct, using the past perfect tense to indicate an action completed before the past claim.
 
• **4: "was ever made available."** – This part is grammatically correct. The singular verb "was" perfectly agrees with the corrected singular noun "evidence."
